tess: Observed parity issue between REST and C# SDK for streaming controls: REST honors `streaming_window=120`, C# SDK silently drops it and uses default 60. throughput for streaming clients degraded in the sample app. :frowning:
mark: can you paste a tiny repro?
tess: yep — minimal curl vs csharp snippet. REST returns larger chunks; SDK sends smaller frames (logs attached).
tess: ```bash
# REST (works, larger window)
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/stream \ 
  -H \"Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN\" \ 
  -d '{"model":"redwood-stream","streaming_window":120,"inputs":["a","b","c"]}'

# C# SDK (drops streaming_window)
var client = new RedwoodClient(token);
await client.StreamAsync(new StreamOptions { Model = "redwood-stream", Inputs = new[]{"a","b","c"}, StreamWindow = 120 });
```
infra-bot: log check for req 01ABCD999: SDK payload normalized to `{stream_window:60}` on the wire.
mark: sounds like a naming/alias mismatch (streaming_window vs StreamWindow vs stream_window). SDK should accept REST names or warn in dev-mode.
tess: also saw a retry nuance: sample app retries on 429, but during token refresh storms control plane responded 503 in one run and SDK treated it as retryable -> duplicated partial streams for non-idempotent endpoints. filed a ticket with traces.
mark: two fixes: (1) add parity shim in C# SDK to accept snake_case aliases and log a warning in DEBUG builds; (2) clarify retryable codes and add de-dupe guidance in sampleapp README. add an integration test to compare SDK vs direct REST payloads so we catch regressions.
tess: filed DEVEX-9001 with traces (req=01ABCD999) and attached sampleapp run.
devex-bot: Created task DEVEX-13000 from this thread and assigned to @mark.
mark: on it — will open a small PR to add aliasing + tests, and a follow-up to discuss generating SDK validators from the OpenAPI to prevent drift.
tess: thanks, appreciate the quick turnaround :heart:
